confirmed_blocking.summary: cmd_checkpoint writes the run state before validating its inputs, and the envelope's bare-JSON path crashes on a missing json import, so every refused or crashed checkpoint leaves the stage advanced, history appended, relay cleared and the worktree uncommitted.
confirmed_blocking.evidence: Reproduced: `checkpoint plan --files nope/missing.txt` exits 1 yet moves stage plan->tasks, appends history 3->4 and clears relay (write_run at commands.py:532 precedes declared_from_envelope at 535 and the missing-path refusal at 539-541); `checkpoint plan --envelope <bare-json-file>` dies with `NameError: name 'json' is not defined` (commands.py:475 calls json.loads; the module imports only os, subprocess, sys, datetime, pathlib) and its state is likewise already advanced. Both paths break the 'a refused write changes nothing' contract asserted in tools/tests/test_commands.py WriterTests.test_checkpoint_refuses_invalid_state_untouched, and replaying the checkpoint double-appends the history entry and re-runs the relay migration. The bare-JSON form is the declared contract of declared_from_envelope (FR-017) but is tested only in the fenced-block form (tools/tests/test_commands.py:555-570); all five dist copies carry the identical code (ENG-17, ENG-26).
confirmed_blocking.fix: Add `import json` to commands.py; resolve and validate the envelope and check every declared path exists before write_run, mutating state and committing only after every refusal point has passed; cover the bare-JSON envelope input with a test.

confirmed_blocking.summary: The run lock gives no mutual exclusion: acquire is check-then-write without exclusive creation and write_state holds the lock only around the final rename while the mutated copy was read long before, so overlapping writers both proceed and the loser's whole-file mutation is silently dropped.
confirmed_blocking.evidence: lock.acquire (lock.py:92-104) reads the lock with read() then writes its own with _write() (plain os.replace of a per-PID temp file, no O_CREAT|O_EXCL), so two processes that both see no live lock both 'acquire'; state.write_state (state.py:360-393) serialises the dict the caller mutated from the copy read in resolve_target and takes the lock only at line 383 around the replace, so even fully serialised writes overwrite each other: last writer wins and the loser's appended history/ledger/verify entry, including the verify-pass record the review gate reads (checks.py), vanishes. FR-005's guarantee is not achieved (ENG-23, ENG-26).
confirmed_blocking.fix: Create the lock atomically (O_CREAT|O_EXCL or link/rename-from-unique-temp), raising LockHeld when it already exists, and hold it across the read-modify-write in write_state (re-read the current state under the lock and re-apply the mutation) instead of only around the rename.

confirmed_blocking.summary: checkpoint migrates relay answers keeping their original timestamps but appends them after every existing decision, so any decision newer than an answer fails validation and the run can never checkpoint again.
confirmed_blocking.evidence: settled_answers (commands.py:447-449) keeps `answer.at` and cmd_checkpoint appends the migrated records at the end of `decisions`; state._check_decisions (state.py:176-177) refuses decreasing times. Reproduced: a decision at 2026-10-23T09:00 plus a relay answer at 2026-10-22T14:05 makes `checkpoint plan` fail with 'decisions[1].at: decisions go backwards in time', and a retry fails identically; FR-001 forbids the only recovery. The shipped fixture dodges the case (tools/tests/test_commands.py writer_state), so the path is untested (ENG-26).
confirmed_blocking.fix: Stamp migrated answers with the checkpoint's own now, or insert them into the decision list in `at` order, so the merged list is always non-decreasing; add a regression test with an answer older than an existing decision.
